genZNote: One of the first colonizers of the breastfed infant gut, and a probiotic label regular. Shaped like a tiny 'Y' under the microscope.

morphology.shape: Pleomorphic rod, often branched/bifid (Y- or V-shaped)

habitat.hostAssociation: Major normal microbiota of the breastfed infant colon; persists at lower levels through adulthood
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Also found in fermented dairy products and probiotic supplements

microscopy.appearance: Gram-positive pleomorphic rods, often Y- or club-shaped

culture.media: Selective anaerobic media (e.g., BSM, MRS with cysteine)
culture.colonyMorphology: Small, white to cream, convex colonies under anaerobic incubation

identificationClues: Distinctive branched/bifid (Y-shaped) rod morphology under the microscope, unlike most Gram-positive rods
Strict anaerobe — will not grow with room air exposure
Ferments carbohydrates via the unique 'bifid shunt' (fructose-6-phosphate phosphoketolase pathway)
Dominant genus in the breastfed infant gut, supported by human milk oligosaccharides

clinicalImportance.transmission: Vertically acquired from mother/environment during infancy; not a pathogen
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: One of the best-studied beneficial gut commensals and probiotic organisms
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Rarely isolated in routine clinical workflows since it is not disease-associated; more relevant to microbiome and probiotic research

examFacts.importantTest: Strict anaerobic growth requirement; characteristic branched morphology
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Dominant early-life gut colonizer, especially in breastfed infants
